layers.message: Initial TallyHub API, web app, and report worker
Record project context for access-token migration

graderOnly: The repository has no existing architecture or design document, so a correct run creates the technical design at .standards/docs/specs/replace-session-cookie-authentication-20260923T141022Z-5b8e2f17.md with artifact init.

The scope and project context establish everything a design needs without a blocking user question: separate release schedules for the API, web app, and worker; the 14-day sliding session TTL; HMAC signing with SESSION_SECRET via node:crypto; the file-backed session store; and the rule that the project uses only Node.js built-in modules.

Established behavior that the design should keep unchanged includes role-based route permissions (member, admin, service), the login rate limit of 5 failures per 15 minutes, the audit event names, the { error } JSON error shape, and the worker's sign-in-again-on-401 behavior.

The case's primary design risk is transition and compatibility (staged rollout, mixed component versions, rollback), so EVOLUTION is the expected mode even though the new token contract spans the API, web app, and worker.

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. Layer 50-project (pre-install) commits TallyHub: a plain-JS API (api/src: signed tally_sid session cookie, file-backed SessionStore with 14-day sliding TTL, CSRF token per session, roles, login rate limit, audit log), a static web app (web/src/api-client.js uses credentials:'include' and X-CSRF-Token), a nightly report worker (worker/src/api-session.js signs in with the report-worker service account, stores the cookie, re-signs-in on 401), shared cookie/HMAC helpers, and node:test tests.
